title: DNS Beaconing — Malicious C2 Domain Detected

fields.summary: During routine DNS traffic analysis, three systems were identified as beaconing to a known malicious C2 domain (meridian-ops.net). The earliest DNS queries trace back 90 days to 07/23/2026. The domain is registered to a known threat actor group operating from Eastern Europe. The beaconing behavior is consistent with a long-term network compromise. No known malware payloads were detected, but the presence of sustained, low-volume DNS tunneling indicates a persistent backdoor.

findings.notes: Three internal hosts (NCIA-PACS-CORE, SEC-SVR-02, NCIA-SEC-DB01) exhibit repeated, non-standard DNS queries to meridian-ops.net, including TXT record requests and subdomain variations.
Hosts NCIA-PACS-CORE and SEC-SVR-02 show beaconing every 3 hours, consistent with C2 communication. No inbound network traffic to these hosts was detected.
Logs from SEC-NVR-01 show DNS requests from 10.66.1.14 (NCIA-PACS-CORE) to meridian-ops.net at 07:23:11, 10:14:22, and 13:01:55 on 07/23/2026 — the first known occurrence.
No file modifications detected on NCIA-PACS-CORE or SEC-SVR-02; no known malicious binaries present.
Pending review; access patterns suggest lateral movement from initial compromise vector.
SEC-BADGE-01 shows no anomalous logins or service interruptions.
All 30-day video recordings are intact and accessible.
Primary and standby database servers show no replication lag or errors.
No unauthorized access attempts recorded in the last 72 hours.
FIDS terminals at Concourse A and B show intermittent display failures, possibly due to network degradation.

actionsTaken: Confirmed malicious domain via VirusTotal and CISA Threat Intelligence feed
Initiated full packet capture on SEC-NVR-01 for forensic retention
Notified IT-Cyber lead via secure chat (10.66.1.55) at 08:09
recommendations: Immediately quarantine all hosts with DNS beaconing behavior
Conduct full forensic analysis of Domain Controller and AODB server
Activate Incident Response Protocol under TIRP Section 13.4
Notify FBI and CISA via secure channel (CISA Case #2026-0777)

instructorNote: This inject establishes the first confirmed evidence of a long-term breach. The IT team must now determine if the attacker is still active and what systems are compromised. Watch for assumptions about network hygiene or confidence in system integrity.
